abstract: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. The best performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train. Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU. On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the best models from the literature. We show that the Transformer generalizes well to other tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both with large and limited training data.

sections.body: The paper states that recurrent networks, such as long short-term memory and gated recurrent models, factor computation along symbol positions. Because each hidden state depends on the previous one, training cannot be parallelized within an example. The authors propose the Transformer, which relies entirely on attention to draw global dependencies between input and output and dispenses with recurrence and convolutions. The text says it can reach a new best result in translation quality after twelve hours of training on eight P100 GPUs.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Recurrent models process positions sequentially, which limits parallelization; the authors propose the Transformer, which uses only attention.

sections.body: The Extended Neural GPU, ByteNet and ConvS2S use convolutions and compute positions in parallel, but the operations needed to relate two positions grow with distance: linearly for ConvS2S and logarithmically for ByteNet. The Transformer reduces this to a constant number, at the cost of reduced effective resolution from averaging attention-weighted positions, which multi-head attention counteracts. The section also covers self-attention used in reading comprehension, summarization and entailment. The authors state the Transformer is the first transduction model relying entirely on self-attention, without sequence-aligned RNNs or convolution.
sections.heading: Background
sections.headline: Prior convolutional models need operations that grow with distance between positions; the Transformer reduces this to a constant number.

sections.body: The encoder and decoder each stack N=6 identical layers. Each encoder layer has multi-head self-attention and a position-wise feed-forward network, with residual connections and layer normalization around each sub-layer. Decoder layers add encoder-decoder attention and mask subsequent positions so predictions depend only on earlier outputs. The model uses 8 heads with `d_k` and `d_v` of 64 and a model dimension of 512. Attention is computed as $\mathrm{softmax}(\frac{QK^{T}}{\sqrt{d_{k}}})V$, with keys scaled by the square root of their dimension. Positional encodings use sine and cosine functions, which the authors hypothesized would allow extrapolation to longer sequences.
sections.heading: Model Architecture
sections.headline: The model stacks six encoder and decoder layers built on scaled dot-product and multi-head attention, with sinusoidal positional encodings.

sections.body: Table 1 compares layer types on per-layer complexity, sequential operations and maximum path length. Self-attention costs O(n^2·d) per layer, uses O(1) sequential operations and has O(1) maximum path length. Recurrent layers cost O(n·d^2) with O(n) sequential operations and O(n) path length. Self-attention is faster than recurrent layers when sequence length n is smaller than dimensionality d, which the authors say is typical for word-piece and byte-pair representations. Restricted self-attention over a neighborhood of size r would raise path length to O(n/r), which the authors leave to future work. The section also argues self-attention may yield more interpretable models.
sections.heading: Why Self-Attention
sections.headline: Self-attention needs a constant number of sequential operations and a constant maximum path length, versus linear for recurrent layers.

sections.body: The English-German data has about 4.5 million sentence pairs with a shared byte-pair vocabulary of about 37000 tokens. The English-French data has 36M sentences and a 32000 word-piece vocabulary. Batches contained approximately 25000 source tokens and 25000 target tokens. Models ran on one machine with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs: base models trained for 100,000 steps or 12 hours, and big models for 300,000 steps or 3.5 days. The optimizer is Adam with beta1 of 0.9, beta2 of 0.98 and epsilon of 10^-9, with `warmup_steps`=4000. Residual dropout uses `P_drop`=0.1 for the base model, and label smoothing uses a value of 0.1.
sections.heading: Training
sections.headline: Models trained on WMT 2014 data with Adam and a warmup learning-rate schedule, using dropout and label smoothing.

sections.body: Table 2 lists BLEU scores and training FLOPs. The big model scores 28.4 on English-to-German, more than 2.0 BLEU above previous models including ensembles, after 3.5 days on 8 P100 GPUs. The base model surpasses all previously published models and ensembles at a fraction of their training cost. The English-to-French text reports 41.0 for the big model, while Table 2 lists 41.8. Table 3 shows single-head attention is 0.9 BLEU worse than the best setting, and learned positional embeddings give nearly identical results. On WSJ section 23, a 4-layer model scores 91.3 F1 when trained on WSJ only and 92.7 semi-supervised.
sections.heading: Results
sections.headline: The big Transformer scores 28.4 BLEU on English-to-German, above prior results including ensembles, and generalizes to parsing.

sections.body: The authors present the Transformer as the first sequence transduction model based entirely on attention, replacing recurrent layers with multi-headed self-attention. They report that it trains significantly faster than recurrent or convolutional architectures. It achieves new results on both WMT 2014 translation tasks and outperforms all previously reported ensembles on English-to-German. Future work includes other input and output modalities such as images, audio and video, local restricted attention for large inputs, and less sequential generation. The paper links to the code used for training and evaluation.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: The authors conclude the Transformer trains faster than recurrent or convolutional models and plan to extend it to other modalities.

sections.body: The appendix shows attention visualizations from encoder self-attention in layer 5 of 6. Figure 3 shows many heads attending from the word 'making' to the distant phrase completing 'making...more difficult'. Figure 4 shows two heads apparently involved in anaphora resolution, with very sharp attention from the word 'its'. Figure 5 gives two examples of heads whose behaviour relates to sentence structure. The authors state the heads clearly learned to perform different tasks.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix shows layer-5 encoder attention heads tracking long-distance verb dependencies, anaphora, and sentence structure.
